short_answer: Sean Murphy is a real, active pick seller. On 17 Nov 2026 PickDawgz listed his plays from 14 to 16 Nov 2026, and Capper Reviews, a site that says it is part of the SportsCapping network, listed his packages. We found no store or company of his own.

Whether his picks make money is a separate question. The sales pages show runs such as "351-272 (+$53.6K for $1K bettors)" on college football sides and a claim of "12 of 17 winning NFL seasons." We found no full, time stamped log of every pick that we could check.

Treat Sean Murphy as a seller with marketing records, not a proven winner. Independent buyer talk is almost absent: three favorable comments on a network owned site, and a forum that bars members from reposting his plays.

guarantee: PickDawgz says that when a "Credit Guaranteed" package does not profit, "a credit for its full purchase price is automatically issued," and that credits "expire 9 months after they are added to your account." It is store credit, not cash, and the passes showed no guarantee wording.

The SportsCapping network, which handles checkout on Capper Reviews, gives free time equal to what you bought if a package loses a single unit, no free time if it made any profit, one free period per purchase, and "There is NO GUARANTEE on seasonal subscriptions." It states: "We do not offer a money back policy like some services do."
Neither version covers your losses on the bets themselves.

claims_note: The start date is not consistent. The bio says 2003, the Capper Reviews year pass copy says he has handicapped professionally "since 2004," and both pages call 2026 his 23rd year.
The college football side run of 351-272 is about 56.3% winners and the totals run of 294-243 about 54.7%. The 57% overall figure on Capper Reviews comes with no count of plays or dates.

The PickDawgz record table covered only a few dozen recent plays (for example 23-8 in college football), so it cannot be squared with the long runs in the package titles. No page shows the underlying list.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every Sean Murphy pick with line, odds and release time, and no court or regulator record about him.

What the sellers publish: runs, unit totals for the last 7 and 30 days, and recent results. On 17 Nov 2026 PickDawgz showed his 10 most recent plays, from 14 to 16 Nov 2026, as 5 wins and 5 losses. The Capper Reviews "yesterday's plays" box showed 4 losses. These are graded by the sites that sell the picks.
We found no outside tally of his plays.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Sean Murphy pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Sean Murphy performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the sellers quote college football runs of about 55% to 56% winners and a 57% overall figure. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Sean Murphy is close to nil. The only buyer comments we found sit on a site that says it is part of the network selling his picks. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found almost no buyer talk about Sean Murphy outside the sites that sell him. Capper Reviews, a network owned site, has three undated comments, all favorable, praising his recent results, a long winning history and detailed free pick write ups. TheRX lists him among paid services members may not repost, which says nothing about quality. Reddit searches for his name only returned posts about the baseball catcher of the same name. We found no complaints about billing or refunds, and no independent record either way.

Capper Reviews shows a rating of 3.73 out of 5 from 22 votes and three undated comments. One calls him the best over the past year, one says he has always been a winner and was among the best on Covers a decade ago, and one praises his free picks and reasoning. The page says he sells through the SportsCapping network, which Capper Reviews is part of, so this is not independent evidence.

TheRX service play guidelines, posted by forum staff, name Sean Murphy in a list of paid services that members should not post in the service play threads. The rule reflects the forum's policy on paid plays, not a judgment of his results.

Reddit archive searches for Sean Murphy in r/sportsbetting, r/SportsBettingPicks and r/sportsbook returned only posts about the MLB catcher Sean Murphy. Our web searches found no Sportsbook Review or Covers thread reviewing the handicapper.

conflicts: Capper Reviews, which hosts the star rating and comments, says it is part of the SportsCapping network that sells his packages, and its purchase links carry affiliate codes.
The Capper Reviews page carried a "$1,000 Free Play at MyBookie" banner linked through an affiliate tracking address. MyBookie is an offshore sportsbook, not licensed by U.S. state regulators.
PickDawgz, which publishes his records and recent results, also sells his packages.
strengths: A named handicapper with a stated history back to 2003 and an active 2026 card.
Prices are published for every package on both storefronts.
The sellers show recent losing results as well as wins, such as the 5 and 5 stretch on PickDawgz.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw comes from a site that sells the picks.
Start year and record figures disagree between pages.
The same passes cost different amounts on the two storefronts.
Guarantees pay in credit or free time, never cash, and season passes have no guarantee.
The main rating page is owned by the selling network and carries an offshore sportsbook affiliate banner.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A run in a package title is not a record.
Count units, not wins. Totals at the wrong number can turn a winning record into a loss.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Here every version is credit or free time.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Compare storefronts before paying. The one year pass was $1,899.95 on one site and $1,999.95 on another.
faq: He is a real, active handicapper whose packages have published prices on established storefronts. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because no site shows a full record of every pick, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Sean Murphy cost?
On 17 Nov 2026 single plays were $40 to $50 on PickDawgz, a 30 day pass was $379.95 there and $374.95 on Capper Reviews, and a one year pass was $1,899.95 or $1,999.95 depending on the site.
Does Sean Murphy have a verified record?

No. The sales pages show runs such as 351-272 on college football sides and a claim of 12 winning NFL seasons out of 17, all published by the sellers. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.

You get every play released in the period you buy, and on some plays a credit or free time if they lose. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays at the lines you can get, and nothing refunds your betting losses.
